thread:
alex_support: FYI escalation from a customer (acct 5421) — after this morning's canary to model v3.2 they're seeing function-call failures. Errors: 422 schema validation and intermittent 401 auth. Billing spike due to retries. Ticket #4521.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: model redwood-v3.2 at 10% in us-east-1 (deploy id: canary-227)

alex_support: Attaching sample payload customer used:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-v3.2",
  "input": "summarize: ...",
  "tools": [{"name": "search", "args": {"q": "pricing changes"}}]
}
```

mira_eng: On it. Any request-id or raw logs from the customer?

alex_support: Customer provided request id req-9f3a2b. Repro steps they sent: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d @payload.json`. They also reported three automatic retry attempts.

jason_sre: Pulled our logs for req-9f3a2b — sequence: 03:22:11 model selection -> redwood-v3.2, tool router chose `search-v2`, then schema validator returned 422: missing required field `filters`. Also saw a 401 for token svc-internal at 03:22:13 — auth proxy returned transient 5xx earlier.

priya_platform: Did we change tool schema mappings in the same deploy? search-v2 requires `filters` where search-v1 did not. That would explain the validator failures.

mira_eng: Confirmed: v3.2 includes a routing heuristic change to prefer v2 tools for performance. That exposes stricter tool schemas. Reproduced locally: pin model to v3.1 -> routes to search-v1 (succeeds); v3.2 -> search-v2 -> 422.

alex_support: Customer also sent a billing graph showing ~3x token usage during retries. They're asking for rollback if this can't be fixed fast.

mira_eng: Short term options: throttle or pause the canary for affected regions, or force tool aliasing so v3.2 picks search-v1 for compatibility. Which is faster?

deploy-bot: canary_update: reducing redwood-v3.2 traffic from 10% -> 0% (pausing) at request of @mira_eng. action id act-3321. Routing reverted to v3.1 for traffic slices impacted.

jason_sre: Auth team notes: the 401s appear to be a separate but coincident issue — token cache TTL bug in auth-proxy triggered under the changed header patterns. Patch queued (auth patch id PATCH-212).

mira_eng: Plan: 1) hotfix tool-routing to respect backward-compatible aliasing (will ship PR), 2) mitigation to force v3.1 tool alias for customers with mixed traffic, 3) coordinate with auth for the cache TTL patch. ETA ~3 hours for hotfix and tests.

alex_support: I'll update the customer: paused canary, routing reverted to v3.1 for their traffic, mitigation rollout in progress. Please drop PR/commit links once available.

mira_eng: PR opened: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/549 (hotfix for routing aliasing). Auth PR: github.com/redwood/auth/pull/212.

jason_sre: Added temporary alert: function-call 422 rate > 0.5% and billing anomaly alert. Will mute noisy alerts until rollback stabilized.

priya_platform: Postmortem items: add schema compatibility checks to canary checklist, run auth header fuzz under canary load, and require explicit tool-schema mapping in model-release notes.

alex_support: Thanks — customer update sent. Keeping ticket #4521 open and monitoring; I'll post status updates here.

ops-bot: note: no customer-facing downtime observed; partial degradation limited to function/tool calls for affected model canary. Tagging #incidents for tracking.

mira_eng: I'll follow up with a postmortem draft after PR merges and monitoring is green. Closing internal escalation thread when we have PRs merged + 2 hours stable metrics.
